key_facts: Grad F presented a sheet containing revised semantic specifications and construction formalisms.
The sheet includes two sides, with one side focusing on semantic specifications and the other on construction formalisms.
Grad F mentioned that the sheet is just one sheet and there are very few changes from previous versions.
Grad F discussed the syntax of the notation, mentioning that the key word is 'construct' followed by a name and type specification.
The concept of 'designate' was discussed, with Grad F explaining it refers to the semantic head of a phrase.
Grad F mentioned that 'semantic constraints' and 'meaning bindings' are used in the notation, though there was some confusion about terminology.
There was a discussion about the use of 'constraints' versus 'bindings', with Grad F suggesting that the term should remain as 'constraints' due to its flexibility.
Grad F explained that the notation allows for both form and meaning types, with the former being more about formal structure and the latter about semantic content.
The group discussed the integration of mental spaces and how they relate to the formalism, with Professor C noting that the mental space concept is not yet fully integrated into the formalism.
Grad F mentioned that the notation includes slots for scenario, referent, discourse segment, and other elements, with the scenario representing the basic predication of an event.
Grad F suggested that the 'scenario' block should be used to represent grammatically specifiable information about a referent, including category, status, and other attributes.
The group discussed the importance of distinguishing between topic and focus in information structure, with Grad F noting that topic is background information and focus is the new information.
Grad F mentioned that the group had previously discussed the use of 'designate' in FrameNet, which refers to required elements in a frame.
Grad F noted that the notation includes a slot for 'predications' which can be used for additional information about a referent.
Grad F proposed that the group should focus on defining the set of constructions they want to develop, rather than attempting to do them in detail at this stage.
Professor C suggested that the group should not attempt to do everything at once and should instead focus on the subset of things they are responsible for.
Grad A mentioned that Eva modified the JavaBayes GUI to include a button for saving data in the embedded JavaBayes format.
Grad A proposed an idea involving probabilistic relational models and Bayes-nets for construal, though it was noted that the models are not currently good enough to implement this idea.
Grad A mentioned that they would prepare a draft of their thesis proposal and present it to the group before leaving.
The group agreed to meet again on Thursday at 1 PM to discuss the thesis proposal and make any necessary changes.
Grad F agreed to the meeting time and mentioned that they would be available for the meeting.
